method: Native Vision face landmarks; inner-mouth height measured perpendicular to eye line and normalized by eye-centroid separation. Eye position/roll measured independently per word. All samples at same local video frame indices.
diagnosis: O does not have a clearly larger sampled peak inner-mouth opening than M. Added hand/eyebrow/head accents are a stronger explanation for perceived emphasis than mouth width alone. Different source framing makes unnormalized comparisons misleading.
independent_visual_review: O combines word shapes with a rising right hand and raised brows around straight, then lifted chin/partly lowered eyelids and hand accent around never. M also moves its chin but lacks visible hand beats.

audio_analysis_only.reason: Owner confirmed visual mouth/head problem; narration remains unchanged.

optional_gain_proposal_if_future_audio_s.interpolation: Smooth raised-cosine ramps in dB; unchanged sample count and timing.
optional_gain_proposal_if_future_audio_s.limits: Only moderates loudness. It cannot remove pitch/duration stress or guarantee different generated movement.

limits: Vision inner-lip landmarks estimate a 2D contour, not true 3D jaw excursion; teeth, facial hair, pose and generation can bias it.
Sparse samples may miss word maxima or brief gestures.
Head metrics measure eye-center displacement and 2D roll, not pitch/yaw.
Face-normalized sheets remove apparent head scale/translation for mouth comparison; head motion must be judged separately.
These measurements support review, not automated acceptance or rejection. M remains the owner-accepted baseline.
